review_notes: Source-first scope decision: the selected family is H1, the full-sample relation between earnings-management magnitude and relationship-specific-investment proxies. Section III calls industry-level variables the “first approach” (p. 7); it calls the identified actual-partner subset the “second approach” (p. 9). Section IV begins “Determinants of Earnings Management Using Industry-Level Variables,” tests H1 by OLS, and presents Table 2 (pp. 13–16). Retain Table 2 Models 1 and 2 as the parallel R&D and alliance/JV proxy specifications.

Exclude Table 2 Models 3–4 because they add Zscore Dummy interactions (financial-health moderation), not additional controls or baseline proxy fits. Exclude Tables 3–4 actual-partner regressions: the paper labels them as a separate second approach and later analysis; pp. 19–20 describe them as addressing potential simultaneity/endogeneity, with smaller supplier/customer samples and only 895 firm-years when both partners’ R&D are measurable. Footnote 18 says Table 2 does not use 2SLS because endogeneity is less relevant for industry-level regressors. The direct-partner/2SLS fits are therefore follow-up analyses, not indispensable components of the selected full-sample H1 design.
Exclude later income-smoothing/large-earnings-increase analyses and H2 consequence/duration outcomes as distinct subsequent questions or decompositions.

The volatility controls require at least five observations, but their estimation-window length is not reported. The alliance/JV proxy counts announcements during 1984–2003, but the paper does not specify the event-year aggregation and denominator year for the firm-year regressions.
